signature: SUBROUTINE DTGSYL( TRANS, IJOB, M, N, A, LDA, B, LDB, C, LDC, D,

params.name: trans
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: solve the generalized Sylvester equation (1).
-   `= 'T'`: solve the 'transposed' system (3).

params.name: ijob
params.reference:
Specifies what kind of functionality to be performed.

-   `= 0`: solve (1) only.
-   `= 1`: The functionality of 0 and 3.
-   `= 2`: The functionality of 0 and 4.
-   `= 3`: Only an estimate of Dif\[(A,D), (B,E)\] is computed. (look ahead strategy `IJOB  = 1` is used).
-   `= 4`: Only an estimate of Dif\[(A,D), (B,E)\] is computed. ( DGECON on sub-systems is used ). Not referenced if `TRANS = 'T'`.

params.name: M
params.reference: The order of the matrices A and D, and the row dimension of the matrices C, F, R and L.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrices B and E, and the column dimension of the matrices C, F, R and L.

params.name: A
params.reference: The upper quasi triangular matrix A.

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1, M)$.

params.name: B
params.reference: The upper quasi triangular matrix B.

params.name: ldb
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array B. $\mathrm{LDB} \ge \max (1, N)$.

params.name: C
params.reference: On entry, C contains the right-hand-side of the first matrix equation in (1) or (3). On exit, if `IJOB = 0`, 1 or 2, C has been overwritten by the solution R. If `IJOB = 3` or 4 and `TRANS = 'N'`, C holds R, the solution achieved during the computation of the Dif-estimate.

params.name: ldc
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array C. $\mathrm{LDC} \ge \max (1, M)$.

params.name: D
params.reference: The upper triangular matrix D.

params.name: ldd
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array D. $\mathrm{LDD} \ge \max (1, M)$.

params.name: E
params.reference: The upper triangular matrix E.

params.name: lde
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array E. $\mathrm{LDE} \ge \max (1, N)$.

params.name: F
params.reference: On entry, F contains the right-hand-side of the second matrix equation in (1) or (3). On exit, if `IJOB = 0`, 1 or 2, F has been overwritten by the solution L. If `IJOB = 3` or 4 and `TRANS = 'N'`, F holds L, the solution achieved during the computation of the Dif-estimate.

params.name: ldf
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array F. $\mathrm{LDF} \ge \max (1, M)$.

params.name: scale
params.reference: On exit `SCALE` is the scaling factor in (1) or (3). If $0 < \mathrm{SCALE} < 1$, C and F hold the solutions R and L, resp., to a slightly perturbed system but the input matrices A, B, D and E have not been changed. If `SCALE = 0`, C and F hold the solutions R and L, respectively, to the homogeneous system with $C = F = 0$. Normally, `SCALE = 1`.

params.name: dif
params.reference: On exit `DIF` is the reciprocal of a lower bound of the reciprocal of the Dif-function, i.e. `DIF` is an upper bound of Dif\[(A,D), (B,E)\] = sigma\_min(Z), where Z as in (2). IF `IJOB = 0` or `TRANS = 'T'`, `DIF` is not touched.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. `LWORK` \> = 1. If `IJOB = 1` or 2 and `TRANS = 'N'`, $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,2 \, M \, N)$.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `=0`: successful exit
-   `<0`: If `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `>0`: (A, D) and (B, E) have common or close eigenvalues.

untranslated: WORK.minLength: local LWMIN is assigned inside nested control flow
